rationale: Hybrid Greek-Coptic compound: Greek prefix ὑπο- ('under, secretly') + Lycopolitan ⲥⲉϫⲉ ('speak'). Denotes one who speaks in private counsel. Listed among Sasanian court officers (magnates, senators, satraps, governors). The verbal use in line 11 governing pronominal object 'me' confirms the agent/verbal sense.
Greek loanword μεγιστᾶνες — the high nobility of the Sasanian court. Distinct from ⲛⲁⲣⲭⲏⲩ 'archons/rulers' (more abstract) and ⲛ̄ⲉⲝⲟⲩⲥⲓⲁⲥⲧⲏⲥ 'powers' (Greek loan for power-bearers).
Greek loanword συγκλητικοί — members of the royal council. Sasanian context: the king's deliberative body.
Greek loanword σατράπης from Old Persian xšaθrapāvan — Persian provincial governors. Standard Sasanian administrative title.
Greek ἡγεμών — provincial leaders, paired with satraps in the standard Sasanian administrative listing.
Lycopolitan ⲍⲛⲧ = Sahidic ϩⲏⲧ 'belly, interior' with 3pl suffix. Used here of the inner counsel-circle of the court. Cf. ⲍⲛ ⲧⲟⲩⲙⲏⲧⲉ 'in their midst' (line 24) as semantic neighbor.
Compound: ⲣⲉϥ- ('one who does') + ⲣ̄- (verbal prefix 'do') + ⲛⲁⲃⲉ ('sin'). The agentive form parallels ⲣⲉϩ†ⲥⲃⲱ 'teacher' confirmed in K.99.

Etymology uncertain. Partially restored as [ⲍⲱ]ⲙϩ in line 13. Context: 'the world loves darkness, hating the ⲍⲱⲙϩ of light.' Suggests an active positive contact-noun. Possible relation to ⲱⲙϩ 'embrace, hold.' Uncertain — flagged for further philological work.
Verb of motion across the sea, used in line 16 with ⲁⲍⲣⲏⲓ̈ ⲍⲛ ⲑⲁⲗⲁⲥⲥⲁ 'up over the sea.' Possibly a reduplicated form related to ⲃⲱⲕ 'go' or a specialized sea-crossing verb. Uncertain.
Lycopolitan reflex of Sahidic ⲧⲁϣⲉⲟⲉⲓϣ 'proclaim, preach.' Standard Manichaean missionary terminology for spreading the message of Truth.
Possible shortened form of ⲟⲩⲉϩⲥⲁϩⲛⲉ 'command, decree' — fits royal-court context. Alternatively ⲟⲩⲏϩ qualitative 'be set, stationed.' Uncertain.
